title: Palette is a fixed scroll of ~38 blocks with no type-to-filter, collapse, or quick-add
existing_state: Palette.tsx renders all block definitions (38 'category:' entries in FlowCanvas/src/blockDefs/registry.ts) across 7 hardcoded categories (Palette.tsx:12-14) as one static scrolling column (Palette.tsx:55-105). There is no filter input, no collapsible category headers, no favorites/recents, and drag-from-palette is the only way to add a block (App.tsx onDrop). A new user hunting for 'extract' or 'portcheck' scans seven category groups; a power user pays the same scroll tax on every single block add. This overlaps the FLOW_CANVAS_ENHANCEMENTS.md roadmap ('Searchable Palette with Icons, Favorites & Recents', lines 158-159; friction acknowledged at line 30) — reported here because the minimal version (a filter box) is a fraction of the roadmap item's scope and removes most of the pain.
recommendation: Add a sticky filter input at the top of Palette.tsx that narrows items by def.label/type/description (case-insensitive substring), hiding empty categories; Escape clears. This is purely local component state — no store or bridge changes. Collapsible category headers and favorites can follow later per the roadmap; the filter alone is the 80% win.
user_benefit: Adding blocks is the single most repeated action when building a preset; type-three-letters-and-drag replaces scanning a 38-item list every time, and newcomers can find blocks by name without learning the category taxonomy first.

evidence.note: hardcoded category order; static list, no input element anywhere in the component
roadmap overlap: Searchable Palette item already planned

mockup_idea: Side-by-side palette rail: current full scroll vs. the same rail with a 'Filter blocks…' input at top showing 'ex' typed and only Extract/Exists/Exit visible under their category headers.
